detail.longDescription: I run a small software agency in Germany. And of course I had some kind of software to manage my projects. It was a very simple ticket tool, and I also did my billing with it. But one day that just annoyed me so much. I mean, you have this problem: a ticket is done. Status set to closed and you've billed it. And then two weeks later the client comes along and wants a small fix for it or a minor change, because maybe something was misunderstood. And with the tool I used, you had to put the ticket back live. But then you didn't know how many hours had already been billed, because ticket closed automatically meant ticket billed. So, and then I built my own tool. And in Lalabase it's like this: You can attach a billing to all elements, to a meeting, to a ticket. To other work. And that's independent of the status the ticket has. What you bill,whether you bill it completely, half, you can see directly on the object every single time. And that way it's no problem to bill work only partially or reopen it later. That's how I started, but then more and more features were added to the project. And honestly, I can't work with a normal classic ticket system anymore, but what I've built now, it is software that has tickets, but it also has all the transcripts from the meetings, has all the notes, has all the documentation, has all the people with contact info, and you have an AI that you can ask across all these things. There's a built-in AI already, but you can also choose your own AI, you can also turn the AI off if you want, and you can also run the whole thing locally with your own AI if you want. Stack: Rails, a single PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Hotwire. AGPL-3.0. Self-host with Docker Compose, or use the hosted version in Germany. Repo: https://github.com/lalabase/lalabase Site: https://lalabase.com/en
